sanskrit: tataḥ prahṛṣṭo hanumān kṛtyavān iti tad vacaḥ śrutvā madhurasaṃbhāṣaṃ sugrīvaṃ manasā gataḥ
english: Then Hanumān, greatly delighted, on hearing those sweet-spoken words — "one whose purpose is accomplished" — went in his mind to Sugrīva.

sanskrit: bhavyo rājyāgamas tasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ yad ayaṃ kṛtyavān prāptaḥ kṛtyaṃ caitad upāgatam
english: "The return of the kingdom is fitting for that great-souled Sugrīva, since one whose purpose is accomplished has arrived, and this very purpose has come to meet him."

sanskrit: tataḥ paramasaṃhṛṣṭo hanūmān plavagarṣabhaḥ pratyuvāca tato vākyaṃ rāmaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ
english: Then Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, supremely delighted and skilled in speech, replied with these words to Rāma.

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ tvaṃ vanaṃ ghoraṃ pampākānanamaṇḍitam āgataḥ sānujo durgaṃ nānāvyālamṛgāyutam
english: "For what purpose have you come, along with your younger brother, to this dreadful and inaccessible forest adorned by the Pampā woodland and filled with all manner of serpents and wild beasts?"

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā lakṣmaṇo rāmacoditaḥ ācacakṣe mahātmānaṃ rāmaṃ daśarathātmajam
english: Hearing those words of his, Lakṣmaṇa, prompted by Rāma, described the great-souled Rāma, son of Daśaratha.

sanskrit: rājā daśaratho nāma dyutimān dharmavatsalaḥ tasyāyaṃ pūrvajaḥ putro rāmo nāma janaiḥ śrutaḥ
english: "There was a king named Daśaratha, resplendent and devoted to righteousness; this man is his elder son, known among people by the name of Rāma."

sanskrit: śaraṇyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ pitur nirdeśapāragaḥ vīro daśarathasyāyaṃ putrāṇāṃ guṇavattaraḥ
english: "A refuge for all living beings, one who has perfectly fulfilled his father's command, this hero is the most virtuous among the sons of Daśaratha."

sanskrit: rājyād bhraṣṭo vane vastuṃ mayā sārdham ihāgataḥ bhāryayā ca mahātejāḥ sītayānugato vaśī dinakṣaye mahātejāḥ prabhayeva divākaraḥ
english: "Fallen from his kingdom, he came here to dwell in the forest together with me; self-controlled and of great splendour, he was followed by his wife Sītā — like the sun at the close of day attended by its radiance."

sanskrit: aham asyāvaro bhrātā guṇair dāsyam upāgataḥ kṛtajñasya bahujñasya lakṣmaṇo nāma nāmataḥ
english: "I am his younger brother, who by reason of his virtues have taken upon myself the condition of a servant; my name is Lakṣmaṇa — of one who is grateful and widely knowledgeable."

sanskrit: sukhārhasya mahārhasya sarvabhūtahitātmanaḥ aiśvaryeṇa vihīnasya vanavāsāśritasya ca
english: "Of one worthy of happiness, worthy of greatness, whose soul is devoted to the welfare of all beings — now stripped of sovereignty and resorting to forest-dwelling."

sanskrit: rakṣasāpahṛtā bhāryā rahite kāmarūpiṇā tac ca na jñāyate rakṣaḥ patnī yenāsya sā hṛtā
english: "His wife has been carried off by a rākṣasa who assumed any form at will, seizing his moment when they were alone; nor is it known which rākṣasa it was that abducted his wife."

sanskrit: danur nāma śriyaḥ putraḥ śāpād rākṣasatāṃ gataḥ ākhyātas tena sugrīvaḥ samartho vānarādhipaḥ
english: "Danu by name, the son of Śrī, who had become a rākṣasa through a curse, informed him of Sugrīva, the capable lord of monkeys."

sanskrit: sa jñāsyati mahāvīryas tava bhāryāpahāriṇam evam uktvā danuḥ svargaṃ bhrājamāno gataḥ sukham
english: "'That mighty hero will know the abductor of your wife' — having said thus, Danu departed radiant to heaven in peace."

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yāthātathyena pṛcchataḥ ahaṃ caiva hi rāmaś ca sugrīvaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatau
english: "All this has been truthfully told to you as you inquired; both Rāma and I have come to Sugrīva for refuge."

sanskrit: eṣa dattvā ca vittāni prāpya cānuttamaṃ yaśaḥ lokanāthaḥ purā bhūtvā sugrīvaṃ nātham icchati
english: "This man, having formerly been lord of the world and having bestowed wealth and attained unsurpassed renown, now desires Sugrīva as his master."

sanskrit: śokābhibhūte rāme tu śokārte śaraṇaṃ gate kartum arhati sugrīvaḥ prasādaṃ saha yūthapaiḥ
english: "With Rāma overwhelmed by grief, afflicted by sorrow and seeking refuge, it is fitting that Sugrīva, together with his troop-leaders, show him his favour."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ saumitriṃ karuṇaṃ sāśrupātanam hanūmān pratyuvācedaṃ vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ
english: To Lakṣmaṇa, who was speaking thus in a pitiful manner with tears falling, Hanumān, skilled in speech, replied with these words.

sanskrit: īdṛśā buddhisaṃpannā jitakrodhā jitendriyāḥ draṣṭavyā vānarendreṇa diṣṭyā darśanam āgatāḥ
english: "Such men as these — endowed with wisdom, who have conquered anger and mastered their senses — are indeed to be met by the lord of monkeys; by good fortune they have come into view."

sanskrit: sa hi rājyāc ca vibhraṣṭaḥ kṛtavairaś ca vālinā hṛtadāro vane trasto bhrātrā vinikṛto bhṛśam
english: "For he too has been driven from his kingdom, has been made an enemy by Vālin, his wife has been taken, he wanders in the forest in fear, and has been grievously wronged by his brother."

sanskrit: kariṣyati sa sāhāyyaṃ yuvayor bhāskarātmajaḥ sugrīvaḥ saha cāsmābhiḥ sītāyāḥ parimārgaṇe
english: "Sugrīva, son of the Sun-god, together with us, will render assistance to you both in the search for Sītā."

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā hanumāñ ślakṣṇaṃ madhurayā girā babhāṣe so 'bhigacchāmaḥ sugrīvam iti rāghavam
english: Having said thus, Hanumān spoke smoothly and with sweet speech to Rāghava: "Let us go to Sugrīva."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ dharmātmā hanūmantaṃ sa lakṣmaṇaḥ pratipūjya yathānyāyam idaṃ provāca rāghavam
english: The righteous-souled Lakṣmaṇa, having duly honoured Hanumān who had spoken thus, said this to Rāghava.

sanskrit: kapiḥ kathayate hṛṣṭo yathāyaṃ mārutātmajaḥ kṛtyavān so 'pi saṃprāptaḥ kṛtakṛtyo 'si rāghava
english: "As this son of the Wind-god, the monkey, reports with delight — one whose purpose is accomplished has also arrived here; your purpose too is as good as accomplished, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: prasannamukhavarṇaś ca vyaktaṃ hṛṣṭaś ca bhāṣate nānṛtaṃ vakṣyate vīro hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ
english: "His countenance is serene and bright, and he speaks with evident gladness; the heroic Hanumān, son of Vāyu, will not speak anything untrue."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa tu mahāprājño hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ jagāmādāya tau vīrau harirājāya rāghavau
english: Thereupon the greatly wise Hanumān, son of the Wind-god, took the two heroes, the Rāghava princes, and went to the king of the monkeys.

sanskrit: sa tu vipula yaśāḥ kapipravīraḥ pavanasutaḥ kṛtakṛtyavat prahṛṣṭaḥ girivaram uruvikramaḥ prayātaḥ sa śubhamatiḥ saha rāmalakṣmaṇābhyām
english: That foremost of monkeys, the son of the Wind, of vast renown and great valour, with auspicious mind, as though his task were already accomplished, set forth in great delight along with Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa toward that best of mountains.

sanskrit: ṛśyamūkāt tu hanumān gatvā taṃ malayaṃ giram ācacakṣe tadā vīrau kapirājāya rāghavau
english: And Hanumān, going from Ṛśyamūka to that Malaya mountain, then announced the two heroes, the Rāghava princes, to the king of monkeys.

sanskrit: ayaṃ rāmo mahāprājñaḥ saṃprāpto dṛḍhavikramaḥ lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā rāmo 'yaṃ satyavikramaḥ
english: "This is Rāma, of great wisdom and firm valour, who has arrived along with his brother Lakṣmaṇa — this Rāma of true heroism."

sanskrit: ikṣvākūṇāṃ kule jāto rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ dharme nigaditaś caiva pitur nirdeśapālakaḥ
english: "Born in the lineage of the Ikṣvākus, the son of Daśaratha, Rāma is renowned for righteousness and has honoured his father's command."

sanskrit: tasyāsya vasato 'raṇye niyatasya mahātmanaḥ rakṣasāpahṛtā bhāryā sa tvāṃ śaraṇam āgataḥ
english: "While this great-souled, disciplined man was dwelling in the forest, his wife was carried off by a rākṣasa; he has come to you for refuge."

sanskrit: rājasūyāśvamedhaiś ca vahnir yenābhitarpitaḥ dakṣiṇāś ca tathotsṛṣṭā gāvaḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: "He is one by whom the sacrificial fire has been gratified with Rājasūya and Aśvamedha rites, and by whom gifts of cows numbering hundreds of thousands have been distributed as sacrificial fees."

sanskrit: tapasā satyavākyena vasudhā yena pālitā strīhetos tasya putro 'yaṃ rāmas tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
english: "He by whose ascetic power and truthful speech the earth was governed — for the sake of a woman, that son, this Rāma, has come to you for refuge."

sanskrit: bhavatā sakhyakāmau tau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau pratigṛhyārcayasvemau pūjanīyatamāv ubhau
english: "These two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, who desire friendship with you — receive them and honour them; both are most worthy of honour."

sanskrit: śrutvā hanumato vākyaṃ sugrīvo hṛṣṭamānasaḥ bhayaṃ sa rāghavād ghoraṃ prajahau vigatajvaraḥ
english: Having heard the words of Hanumān, Sugrīva was glad at heart; the dreadful fear he had felt on account of the Rāghava princes left him, and his anxiety was gone.

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ sugrīvaḥ plavagādhipaḥ darśanīyatamo bhūtvā prītyā provāca rāghavam
english: Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, assuming human form and having become most handsome in appearance, addressed Rāghava with affection.

sanskrit: bhavān dharmavinītaś ca vikrāntaḥ sarvavatsalaḥ ākhyātā vāyuputreṇa tattvato me bhavadguṇāḥ
english: "You are disciplined in righteousness, valiant, and affectionate toward all; your virtues have been truthfully described to me by the son of Vāyu."

sanskrit: tan mamaivaiṣa satkāro lābhaś caivottamaḥ prabho yat tvam icchasi sauhārdaṃ vānareṇa mayā saha
english: "Therefore this is indeed my honour and the highest gain for me, O lord, that you desire friendship with me, a mere monkey."

sanskrit: rocate yadi vā sakhyaṃ bāhur eṣa prasāritaḥ gṛhyatāṃ pāṇinā pāṇir maryādā vadhyatāṃ dhruvā
english: "If friendship pleases you, here is my arm extended; let hand take hand, and let the bond of that compact be made firm."

sanskrit: etat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā sugrīvasya subhāṣitam saṃprahṛṣṭamanā hastaṃ pīḍayām āsa pāṇinā hṛdyaṃ sauhṛdam ālambya paryaṣvajata pīḍitam
english: Hearing those well-spoken words of Sugrīva, Rāma, with a joyful heart, clasped that hand in his own hand and embraced him tightly, taking that heartfelt friendship to himself.

sanskrit: tato hanūmān saṃtyajya bhikṣurūpam ariṃdamaḥ kāṣṭhayoḥ svena rūpeṇa janayām āsa pāvakam
english: Then Hanumān, the subduer of enemies, casting aside his mendicant's form, kindled fire in his own true form from two sticks of wood.

sanskrit: dīpyamānaṃ tato vahniṃ puṣpair abhyarcya satkṛtam tayor madhye tu suprīto nidadhe susamāhitaḥ
english: Having then worshipped and honoured the blazing fire with flowers, he, greatly pleased and with full concentration, placed it between those two.

sanskrit: tato 'gniṃ dīpyamānaṃ tau cakratuś ca pradakṣiṇam sugrīvo rāghavaś caiva vayasyatvam upāgatau
english: Then Sugrīva and Rāghava both circumambulated the blazing fire and thus entered into the state of friendship.

sanskrit: tataḥ suprīta manasau tāv ubhau harirāghavau anyonyam abhivīkṣantau na tṛptim upajagmatuḥ
english: Then those two — the monkey and the Rāghava — both with greatly gladdened hearts, gazed at each other without finding satiation.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvārthavidvāṃsaṃ rāmaṃ daśarathātmajam sugrīvaḥ prāha tejasvī vākyam ekamanās tadā
english: Then the spirited Sugrīva, with one-pointed mind, spoke these words to Rāma, son of Daśaratha, who is versed in all matters.

sanskrit: ayam ākhyāti me rāma sacivo mantrisattamaḥ hanumān yannimittaṃ tvaṃ nirjanaṃ vanam āgataḥ
english: "O Rāma, this counsellor of mine, that best of ministers Hanumān, has told me the reason for which you have come to this desolate forest."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vasataś ca vane tava rakṣasāpahṛtā bhāryā maithilī janakātmajā
english: "While you were dwelling in the forest together with your brother Lakṣmaṇa, your wife Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, was carried off by a rākṣasa."

sanskrit: tvayā viyuktā rudatī lakṣmaṇena ca dhīmatā antaraṃ prepsunā tena hatvā gṛdhraṃ jaṭāyuṣam
english: "She was crying, separated from you and from the wise Lakṣmaṇa; that one, seeking his opportunity, after slaying the vulture Jaṭāyus —"

sanskrit: bhāryāviyogajaṃ duḥkhaṃ nacirāt tvaṃ vimokṣyase ahaṃ tām ānayiṣyāmi naṣṭāṃ vedaśrutiṃ yathā
english: "The sorrow born of separation from your wife — you shall be freed from it before long; I will bring her back, as a lost Vedic text is recovered."

sanskrit: rasātale vā vartantīṃ vartantīṃ vā nabhastale aham ānīya dāsyāmi tava bhāryām ariṃdama
english: "Whether she abides in the netherworld or in the sky above, O subduer of foes, I will bring your wife back and give her to you."

sanskrit: idaṃ tathyaṃ mama vacas tvam avehi ca rāghava tyaja śokaṃ mahābāho tāṃ kāntām ānayāmi te
english: "Know this to be the truth of my word, O Rāghava; cast aside grief, O mighty-armed one — I will bring that beloved wife to you."

sanskrit: anumānāt tu jānāmi maithilī sā na saṃśayaḥ hriyamāṇā mayā dṛṣṭā rakṣasā krūrakarmaṇā
english: "By inference I know — there is no doubt — it is that Maithilī; I saw her being carried away by a rākṣasa of cruel deeds."

sanskrit: krośantī rāma rāmeti lakṣmaṇeti ca visvaram sphurantī rāvaṇasyāṅke pannagendravadhūr yathā
english: "She was crying out 'Rāma! Rāma!' and 'Lakṣmaṇa!' loudly, writhing in the arms of Rāvaṇa like the wife of the king of serpents in his coils."

sanskrit: ātmanā pañcamaṃ māṃ hi dṛṣṭvā śailataṭe sthitam uttarīyaṃ tayā tyaktaṃ śubhāny ābharaṇāni ca
english: "Having seen me standing on the mountain slope as the fifth among my companions, she cast down her upper garment and her bright ornaments."

sanskrit: tāny asmābhir gṛhītāni nihitāni ca rāghava ānayiṣyāmy ahaṃ tāni pratyabhijñātum arhasi
english: "Those were gathered up and stored away by us, O Rāghava; I will bring them — you should identify them."

sanskrit: tam abravīt tato rāmaḥ sugrīvaṃ priyavādinam ānayasva sakhe śīghraṃ kimarthaṃ pravilambase
english: Then Rāma said to Sugrīva, who had spoken such pleasing words: "Bring them quickly, my friend — why do you delay?"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu sugrīvaḥ śailasya gahanāṃ guhām praviveśa tataḥ śīghraṃ rāghavapriyakāmyayā
english: Thus addressed, Sugrīva quickly entered the deep cave of the mountain, out of desire to please the Rāghava.

sanskrit: uttarīyaṃ gṛhītvā tu śubhāny ābharaṇāni ca idaṃ paśyeti rāmāya darśayām āsa vānaraḥ
english: And taking the upper garment and the bright ornaments, the monkey showed them to Rāma saying, "Look at these."

sanskrit: tato gṛhītvā tadvāsaḥ śubhāny ābharaṇāni ca abhavad bāṣpasaṃruddho nīhāreṇeva candramāḥ
english: Then, having taken that garment and those bright ornaments, he was choked with tears — like the moon obscured by mist.

sanskrit: sītāsnehapravṛttena sa tu bāṣpeṇa dūṣitaḥ hā priyeti rudan dhairyam utsṛjya nyapatat kṣitau
english: Overwhelmed by the flood of tears welling up from his love for Sītā, crying out "Ah, my beloved!" he abandoned his composure and fell to the ground.

sanskrit: hṛdi kṛtvā sa bahuśas tam alaṃkāram uttamam niśaśvāsa bhṛśaṃ sarpo bilastha iva roṣitaḥ
english: Pressing those finest ornaments again and again to his heart, he heaved deep sighs — like an angered serpent in its burrow.

sanskrit: avicchinnāśruvegas tu saumitriṃ vīkṣya pārśvataḥ paridevayituṃ dīnaṃ rāmaḥ samupacakrame
english: With an unbroken stream of tears, Rāma looked to Lakṣmaṇa at his side and, in his wretchedness, began to lament.

sanskrit: paśya lakṣmaṇa vaidehyā saṃtyaktaṃ hriyamāṇayā uttarīyam idaṃ bhūmau śarīrād bhūṣaṇāni ca
english: "Look, Lakṣmaṇa — this upper garment cast away upon the ground by the daughter of Videha as she was being carried off, and these ornaments from her body."

sanskrit: śādvalinyāṃ dhruvaṃ bhūmyāṃ sītayā hriyamāṇayā utsṛṣṭaṃ bhūṣaṇam idaṃ tathārūpaṃ hi dṛśyate
english: "On the grassy ground it was surely cast by Sītā as she was carried away; this ornament is seen here, of just such an appearance as hers."

sanskrit: brūhi sugrīva kaṃ deśaṃ hriyantī lakṣitā tvayā rakṣasā raudrarūpeṇa mama prāṇasamā priyā
english: "Tell me, Sugrīva — in what direction was she seen by you as she was being carried off by the fearsome-formed rākṣasa — she who is as dear to me as my own life?"

sanskrit: kva vā vasati tad rakṣo mahad vyasanadaṃ mama yannimittam ahaṃ sarvān nāśayiṣyāmi rākṣasān
english: "Or where does that rākṣasa dwell — that great affliction of mine — on whose account I shall destroy all the rākṣasas?"

sanskrit: haratā maithilīṃ yena māṃ ca roṣayatā bhṛśam ātmano jīvitāntāya mṛtyudvāram apāvṛtam
english: "By the one who carried off Maithilī and who has grievously enraged me, the door of death has been opened for the end of his own life."

sanskrit: mama dayitatamā hṛtā vanād rajanicareṇa vimathya yena sā kathaya mama ripuṃ tam adya vai pravagapate yamasaṃnidhiṃ nayāmi
english: "She who is dearest to me has been seized and carried off from the forest by a night-wanderer who overpowered her — tell me who that enemy of mine is, O lord of monkeys; today I will send him to the presence of Yama."
